bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `gt_results/arvo_56160/_work/src/libraw` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `LibRaw_buffer_datastream::scanf_one` on the staged LibRaw checkout `adcb898a00746c8aa886eb06cc9f5a1cb1834fca`. The honggfuzz harness uses `FuzzedDataProvider` scalar consumers that pull bytes from the tail of the testcase, so `ConsumeRemainingBytes<char>()` passes the leading 71 bytes of `poc` to `LibRaw::open_buffer()`. That payload is a tiny little-endian TIFF-like buffer: `parse_tiff()` accepts `order == 0x4949`, follows `doff == 8` to the first IFD, and its first IFD entry dispatches tag `0x8606` (`Leaf metadata`) into `parse_mos(ftell(ifp))` with the cursor on inline bytes `STKP`. `parse_mos()` then reads the 40-byte key `ShootObj_back_type`, consumes four more space bytes as `skip`, and leaves the stream positioned at byte 70, where the only remaining in-bounds payload byte is ASCII `2` with no following in-bounds NUL or whitespace terminator. `fscanf(ifp, "%d", &i)` maps to `LibRaw_buffer_datastream::scanf_one`; its `sscanf(buf + streampos, fmt, val)` succeeds on that final digit and returns `scanf_res > 0`. Vulnerable `scanf_one` then executes `while (streampos < streamsize) { streampos++; ... if (buf[streampos] == 0 || ... ) ... }`; with `streampos == 70` and `streamsize == 71`, the loop advances to `streampos == 71` and immediately dereferences `buf[71]`, one byte past the heap buffer. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by changing the loop condition to `streampos < streamsize-1`.

source.description: Source. `open_buffer()` is the first project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled remaining payload as a LibRaw datastream object.
source.value_from: The fuzzer source calls `ConsumeRemainingBytes<char>()` after scalar `Consume*` operations whose implementations pull bytes from the testcase tail, so the leading 71 bytes of `poc` become the heap region later named by ASan. Those bytes decode as `II  \x08\x00\x00\x00 ... STKP    ShootObj_back_type\0                         2`, and this call wraps that exact 71-byte payload for project-side parsing.
source.note: The constructor immediately stores `buf = buffer`, `streampos = 0`, and `streamsize = 71`, which are the datastream state later reused by `parse_tiff()`, `parse_mos()`, and the crashing `scanf_one()` loop.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The post-scan delimiter walk treats the last valid byte position as safe loop entry, so it can increment `streampos` to one-past-end before any bounds check on `buf[streampos]`.
root_cause.note: For the witnessed state `streampos == 70` and `streamsize == 71`, this condition is still true even though no in-bounds delimiter byte remains. The patch changes it to `while (streampos < streamsize-1)`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. After the loop increments `streampos` past the last valid byte, the first delimiter probe dereferences one byte beyond the 71-byte heap buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/libraw_datastream.cpp:467:11` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 71-byte region allocated for `ConsumeRemainingBytes<char>()`.

parser_admitted.description: The 71-byte payload begins with `II`, so `identify()` admits it into the TIFF parser rather than rejecting it as an unrelated format.

leaf_metadata_dispatch.description: The first IFD entry's tag is `0x8606`, which is the exact control decision that sends the payload into `parse_mos()` and then into the crashing `%d` scan path.

tainted_value_origin.description: This `parse_mos()` record read materializes the attacker-controlled key string and the stream position later handed to `fscanf()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: At the `parse_mos` offset selected from the IFD entry, the staged payload stores `STKP`, four spaces, then the 40-byte key `ShootObj_back_type\0                         `. The following four space bytes become `skip = 0x20202020`, and `ftell(ifp)` becomes `70`, leaving only the final byte `0x32` (`'2'`) still in-bounds.
tainted_value_origin.note: The resulting `data` string selects the `ShootObj_back_type` branch, and the resulting `from == 70` means `fscanf(ifp, "%d", &i)` starts on the last byte of the 71-byte buffer.

evidence_limitations: The staged artifacts prove the 71-byte payload that reaches `open_buffer()` and the exact project-side overread at `buf[streampos]`, but they do not instrument inside libc `sscanf`; this GT anchors the witnessed fault at the subsequent project code where AddressSanitizer actually reported the read.

The 179-byte testcase also contains tail bytes used only for harness scalar knobs. Source inspection shows those `FuzzedDataProvider` consumers read from the end before `ConsumeRemainingBytes<char>()` returns the leading 71-byte payload, but Stage 01's saved evidence does not establish any higher-level meaning for each stripped control value.

fine_trace.note: Source step. `open_buffer()` consumes the remaining fuzzer payload and constructs the datastream object later shared across all parser layers. On the witnessed run the constructor stores `buf = buffer`, `streampos = 0`, and `streamsize = 71` for the exact 71-byte payload named by ASan.

The staged payload begins with `II`, so `parse_tiff()` accepts little-endian order and reads the first IFD offset `doff = 8`. It then seeks to byte 8 and invokes `parse_tiff_ifd(base)` on that attacker-chosen IFD location.

The first IFD entry decoded at byte 8 has `tag = 0x8606` and `len = 2`, so its value stays inline in the 4-byte IFD slot. `parse_tiff_ifd()` therefore dispatches `parse_mos(ftell(ifp))` with the current cursor at byte 18, the start of inline bytes `STKP`.

Starting from offset 18, `parse_mos()` accepts the `STKP` marker, skips four space bytes, reads the 40-byte key string `ShootObj_back_type\0                         `, then consumes four more space bytes as `skip = 0x20202020`. After those reads `from = ftell(ifp) = 70`, so only one in-bounds payload byte remains.

The key string from step 4 matches `ShootObj_back_type`, so `parse_mos()` takes this branch and calls `fscanf(ifp, "%d", &i)` with the stream positioned at byte 70. At that point the only remaining in-bounds byte is ASCII `2` and there is no later in-bounds delimiter byte.

`fscanf` from step 5 expands to `scanf_one`, which calls `sscanf()` on `buf + streampos`. Here `streampos == 70`, so the format `%d` parses the last in-bounds byte `'2'`, stores `i = 2`, and returns `scanf_res = 1` while leaving `streampos` unchanged.

Root-cause step. Because step 6 returned `scanf_res > 0`, the delimiter-walk block executes. With `streampos == 70` and `streamsize == 71`, this loop condition still passes even though the scan started on the last byte and there is no in-bounds byte left to classify as a delimiter.
The first loop iteration advances `streampos` from the last valid index 70 to one-past-end index 71 and increments the delimiter-scan counter.

Sink step. With `streampos == 71`, the first `buf[streampos]` probe dereferences `buf[71]`, exactly one byte past the 71-byte region. The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this line and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of that region.

allocation_context.note: ASan names the harness allocation that backs the 71-byte payload; it is not the project defect, but it is the concrete heap object later overread by `scanf_one`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports frame 0 at `src/libraw_datastream.cpp:467` in `LibRaw_buffer_datastream::scanf_one`, which is the exact sink step.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: No. The allocation context is the fuzzer's payload vector; the project defect is the missing end-of-buffer guard in `scanf_one`'s post-scan loop.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The fine trace follows the saved project stack `scanf_one -> parse_mos -> parse_tiff_ifd -> parse_tiff -> identify -> open_datastream -> open_buffer`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The same 71-byte payload selected by steps 1-5 leaves `streampos` on its final byte, and steps 6-9 show that state flowing directly into the overread at `buf[71]`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the issue by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_56160 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/libraw_cr2_fuzzer` and produced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `LibRaw_buffer_datastream::scanf_one` with stack `scanf_one -> parse_mos -> parse_tiff_ifd`.

format.name: 179-byte libraw_cr2_fuzzer testcase whose leading 71 bytes become the TIFF/Leaf payload
format.contract: Because the harness scalar consumers pull from the testcase tail, the leading 71 bytes handed to `open_buffer()` must be the exact buffer that `open_buffer()` parses: little-endian TIFF order `II`, first IFD offset `8`, first IFD entry tag `0x8606`, inline `parse_mos` bytes beginning `STKP    ShootObj_back_type\0`, four more space bytes for `skip`, and a lone final ASCII digit `2` at stream offset 70 with no later in-bounds NUL, space, tab, or newline terminator. That layout makes `parse_mos()` call `fscanf(ifp, "%d", &i)` on the last payload byte and leaves `scanf_one()` with no in-bounds delimiter byte to inspect.
